newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan warns mutual funds not to manipulate stocks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan warns mutual funds not to manipulate stocks.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission has warned chief executives of 20 securities investment trust firms not to manipulate stocks, the Economic Daily News said on Wednesday.

The commission called the executives to a meeting late on Tuesday and urged them not to become involved in management of listed firms and not to cooperate with major market players to manipulate stock prices, the paper said.
Two commission officials reached by Reuters said the commission had held a seminar with local securities trust firms on Tuesday but declined to confirm all the details.
The warning was issued after Taiwan's stock market turnover on Tuesday hit an all-time high of T$238.9 billion.
On Tuesday, the benchmark index ended down 57.07 points or 0.67 percent at 8,460.63, off an intraday high of 8,624.78 that was the market's highest level in nearly seven years.
The warning was the second in a row after the SEC on March 20 sent a letter to the island's securities brokerages, urging them to protect investors' rights after recent market rallies.
Brokers said the move was intended to cool the market.
"Apparently, the SEC does not want to see an overheated market. It wants to cool down the market," said Nomura Securities research chief Ben Lee.
